claim: Natural slate resists New Jersey freeze-thaw cycling through near-zero water absorption
suggestedFix: Drop 'near-zero water absorption.' Reframe to the pack-supported fact: slate's stone outlasts its fasteners/flashing, so freeze-thaw failures trace to corroded fasteners and degraded valley flashing rather than the stone (facts-materials-economics.md:117, NRCA/NSA). Replace comparisonRows[4].itemB with e.g. 'Stone unaffected; failures are fasteners/flashing — NRCA/NSA.'

claim: ...crack and curl after years of freeze-thaw, especially lower-grade 3-tab, per InterNACHI failure-mode guidance.
suggestedFix: Re-attribute the asphalt curl/crack failure mode to 'NRCA and InterNACHI guidance' (matching facts-materials-economics.md:81) and remove the slate 'near-zero water absorption per InterNACHI' clause entirely, since InterNACHI supplies no such property.

claim: with weathering limited to surface sugaring on lower-grade stone rather than structural cracking, per NPS Preservation Brief 29.
suggestedFix: Attribute sugaring to 'NRCA and the National Slate Association' (its source at facts-materials-economics.md:117). Drop or qualitatively reframe 'holds its surface against November-through-March freeze cycles,' since no pack ties a freeze-cycle-resistance claim to slate or to Brief 29.

claim: Asphalt shingles depend on an ice-and-water shield underlayment at the eaves, required by the NJ Uniform Construction Code, to block ice-dam backup...
suggestedFix: Scope and cite to the pack: 'an ice-and-water shield is required at eaves with an ice-dam history, extending at least 24 in. inside the exterior wall line, per IRC R905.1.2 as enforced under the NJ Uniform Construction Code (N.J.A.C. 5:23).'

claim: slate requires confirmed structural capacity that many post-1960 NJ homes and additions lack
suggestedFix: Remove the fabricated 'post-1960 NJ homes' threshold and the absolute 'confirmed framing required' framing. Either drop the structural-capacity claim or state slate's weight qualitatively only after adding a sourced slate-weight figure (lb/sq ft) with a named source to a pack.
